north_star.goal: Produce high-quality CET4/CET6 cards that help Chinese college students pass the exam through micro-coaching card learning.

default_user_model.primary_group: Chinese college students preparing for CET4/CET6

coverage_policy.single_card_goal_policy: Each card must have exactly one main training goal and may have secondary goals.
coverage_policy.box_quality_policy: A formal candidate box must show progression from recognition to application to transfer, and must avoid repetition and gaps.

difficulty_policy.card_assignment: A card must have one primary difficulty tier and may have secondary tiers.
difficulty_policy.cet4_cet6_relationship: CET4 and CET6 may share structure, but CET6 must raise language, inference, and expression difficulty.
difficulty_policy.advanced_card_in_foundation_phase: Allowed only when labeled and justified.

candidate_integrity_policy.authority_boundary: This workspace may enforce stricter candidate integrity than the product runtime, but canonical interaction semantics remain owned by ../softbook_cet/spec/interactions.json.
candidate_integrity_policy.runtime_projection_privacy: Current runtime identity derivation traverses every projected card and rejects exact authoring-only prompt, model, harness, credential, token, secret, API-key, and private-key fields. Review and execution evidence remains outside the product card payload.
candidate_integrity_policy.legacy_metadata_compatibility: Untouched legacy cards may omit quality_metadata; any card that already carries quality_metadata must conform to spec/card-metadata.schema.json, and any added or modified candidate card must carry conforming quality_metadata without grandfathering inherited defects.
candidate_integrity_policy.changed_candidate_detection: Derive added or modified card objects by card_id from the merge-base-to-head Git diff; every file consumed under card_boxes_json must use the canonical governed filename, and declared review scope is evidence but cannot narrow the validator's discovered card set.
candidate_integrity_policy.governed_review_path_detection: Every JSON change under active review, authorization, draft, or scoped-audit directories triggers content-candidate validation by exact prefix/suffix classification without relying on a four-digit box prefix. Historical v1 person-authority directories remain immutable archive surfaces and never create current authorization. Governed records must be direct regular JSON children of their declared directories and nested records fail closed. Git paths are preserved exactly; literal backslashes, controls, and Unicode line separators are rejected rather than rewritten. Git handoffs remain classified by their governed content scope rather than treating every delivery-only handoff as content.
candidate_integrity_policy.current_scoped_audit_snapshot: Replay the current audit against the complete card_boxes_json tree materialized from the immutable HEAD commit, including deletions and rename sources; overlay only the current audit harness and never leave base-only card files in the temporary audit worktree.

self_review_parity.standard_review_per_card_coverage: Every added or modified card has exactly one current model-owned snapshot whose interaction_id, knowledge_ref, quality metadata, answer truth, and source references match its unique immutable HEAD corpus card. Batch generation does not pause for a separate confirmation state.
self_review_parity.standard_review_batch_conclusion: batch_review must carry non-empty box_progression, an explicit repetition_or_gap_risks array, non-empty unique representative_cards contained in scope.card_ids, and non-empty next_step before standard snapshots count
self_review_parity.current_scoped_audit_required: every new or changed standard, residual-closure, or full-track review or approval record must link one direct current report under reviews/audit_scopes; the global report may be referenced only by byte-for-byte immutable records named by the immutable pre-cutover index
self_review_parity.scoped_audit_artifact_integrity: every new or changed direct scoped-audit JSON blob must exactly equal a current immutable-HEAD audit replay for its declared scope, even when no review links it; standalone harness validation rejects malformed tracked artifacts, replays current-fingerprint artifacts, permits structurally valid unchanged historical fingerprints, and hash-pins the explicit legacy exception; historical approval remains archive evidence, and current-fingerprint evidence counts as current authorization only after the consumer independently regenerates the complete current audit and exactly replays both scoped reports
self_review_parity.historical_self_review_lifecycle: an unchanged historical self-review linked to an unchanged historical scoped report is historical evidence, not current authorization; validate it against its recorded report fingerprint and rule set without requiring current-card snapshot or current-track parity, while PR-scope validation requires every changed review to use current immutable-HEAD replay and parity
self_review_parity.current_approval_authorization: Queue and release-gap consumers may count a formal authorization only when the direct canonical non-template authorization, direct linked model review, both scoped reports, active audit script, and active audit rule spec are regular committed records or authority whose worktree, index, and one fixed HEAD modes and bytes agree. The authorization must have complete formal fields and exact scope, its direct scoped audit must exactly replay the complete current card-quality audit, and its direct canonical complete linked review must have matching scope, model-accepted semantics, and a scoped audit that also exactly replays the complete current audit. Full-track authorization must bind one direct immutable runtime payload or one direct immutable shard manifest and its SHA-256. Manifest shards must be direct regular JSON files whose exact bytes, counts, order, and non-overlapping card ranges are bound and captured in the same fixed snapshot. Validators reconstruct the normalized payload, derive the canonical content_version, require exact track/card scope, and include both that version and the direct payload or manifest byte SHA-256 in buildModelAcceptanceInputSha256 additionalBindings for both independent acceptance runs. Ordinary scoped authorization is not forced to name a runtime version that does not exist yet. Before returning, the consumer rechecks the fixed HEAD/index snapshot, all captured authority/evidence and shard modes and bytes, and the corpus fingerprint. Merely being tracked, matching only a current corpus digest, using a self-declared summary, or claiming zero blockers is insufficient. Historical approvals remain archive evidence and templates, traversal, symlinks, incomplete records, historical approvals, dirty/staged/mode-drifted authority, manifest or shard evidence, concurrent snapshot drift, forged or stale audits, stale linked reviews, missing runtime-payload bindings, missing or replayed shards, or cross-version acceptance replay never count as current authorization.
self_review_parity.residual_closure_boundary: residual blocker closure requires explicit sample_policy.review_scope_type=residual_blocker_closure plus a direct current scoped audit, may cover only modified pre-existing cards, and cannot authorize newly added card generation
self_review_parity.quality_metadata_comparison: deep semantic equality of every quality_metadata field except review_status in both PR-scope validation and standalone harness validation; object key order is irrelevant while array order and absent-versus-present fields remain significant
self_review_parity.review_status_semantics: card corpus and self-review artifacts carry different lifecycle views (for example card=draft while review snapshot=agent_pass), so each review_status is validated independently and is the only parity exclusion
self_review_parity.full_track_aggregate_boundary: A current full-track record is aggregate model-review evidence bound to one model-acceptance.v2 actor/evidence object, a direct current scoped audit, exact complete-track card and box scope, complete quality_audit summary, non-empty representative cards, and an accepted decision. Scope and coverage IDs remain identical and every covered ID resolves uniquely in immutable HEAD. Any removal must use governed destructive-change evidence rather than being hidden by aggregate coverage.

candidate_integrity_policy.review_authority_artifact_integrity: Current review, content-authorization, runtime-payload binding, and audio-acceptance templates are regular files whose complete governed shapes include model-acceptance.v2 evidence. Current authorization requires a timezone-qualified review time, exact input SHA-256, real agent/model/run identity, required capabilities, an accepted decision, non-empty exact scope, and current audit replay. The governed full-track authorization shape also requires a direct rehashed runtime payload or direct rehashed shard manifest, every manifest shard captured and rehashed in the same fixed snapshot, recomputed canonical content_version, and both single-task context-perturbation model inputs bound to that version plus the direct payload or manifest byte SHA-256. Existing v1 person-authority artifacts remain immutable archive evidence only.

elimination_integrity.canonical_item_shape: {id,text}; changed candidates require an explicit non-empty unique id, while the formal runtime bridge normalizes untouched legacy items with item.id ?? item.text
elimination_integrity.legacy_preview_projection: eliminable_items stays the local text/is_correct preview projection; each entry aligns by position and text with elimination_items, and is_correct must equal membership of that canonical runtime ID in answer_key.correct_items
elimination_integrity.untouched_legacy_compatibility: The current migrated corpus may retain text/is_correct entries in both fields and text-as-ID correct_items only in global read-only validation; any added or modified candidate must upgrade to explicit runtime IDs.
elimination_integrity.answer_truth: answer_key.correct_items must equal the unique runtime IDs selected by the preview projection; order alone is not significant

back_side_analysis_policy.answer_explanation: Required when the card prototype or interaction asks for a specific answer.

source_policy.true_exam_role: High-quality source and calibration reference, not the only source.

tts_policy.candidate_audio_boundary: Existing TTS assets may support candidate sample review only when marked sample-only; formal audio readiness requires reviews/audio_qc evidence.

blockers.description: Answer, reasoning, or explanation is contradictory or likely to mislead the learner, including wrong option letters, nonexistent word-bank items, or a distractor explanation attached to the wrong labeled choice.
Chinese explanation is awkward enough to harm learning, or English content is unnatural, ungrammatical, or Chinese-English.
Wording is unclear, misleading, over-marketing, motivational filler, or not suitable for CET learning.
Content only repeats the prompt or answer, says generic reminders, lacks mechanism, or has no transfer/exam value.
The card does not satisfy the user task, softbook_cet product spec, or library/group/box target.
The front side is derived from back-side answer or analysis instead of standing as an independent learning input.
AI-generated, rewritten, simulated, or human-original material is presented as true exam material.
Cards are repeated low-quality variants produced to fill a batch rather than serve real progression.

severity_policy.major: Can be preserved as draft but must be reworked.
severity_policy.minor: May be fixed after review if it does not affect learning correctness or product fit.
severity_policy.batch_threshold: Any blocker blocks the card; more than one major issue sends the card to revise.
